lessons.title: The Second World War, the UN and trusteeship

objectives: Explain the causes of the Second World War in outline
Describe the war and Cameroon's role
Explain the creation of the United Nations
Explain the trusteeship system and its effect on African nationalism

blocks.md: The **Second World War** (**1939–1945**) was the largest war in history. After the First World War, economic depression, bitterness over the peace treaties, the rise of dictators such as **Hitler** in Germany, aggressive policies by Italy and Japan, and the weakness of the League of Nations led to war. It began in **September 1939** when Germany invaded Poland and Britain and France declared war. It ended in Europe in **May 1945** and in Asia in **August–September 1945**.

blocks.caption: The Second World War and after
blocks.alt: A timeline from 1939 to 1948 with 1939, 1945 and 1946 and the period of the war.

blocks.title: Cameroon in the war
blocks.md: In **1940**, French Cameroun rallied to the **Free French** movement of General de Gaulle, becoming a base in Equatorial Africa. Many Cameroonians served as soldiers and carriers, and the territory supplied **rubber, cocoa, timber, bananas, palm products** and other goods for the Allied war effort. British Cameroons also supplied goods and men. The war brought shortages, higher prices, and forced contributions, but also new ideas about freedom.

blocks.title: The United Nations
blocks.md: The **United Nations (UN)** was founded in **1945**, after the war, to maintain **peace and security**, promote **human rights** and encourage cooperation. Its main bodies include the **General Assembly**, the **Security Council** and the **Trusteeship Council**. The League's former mandates became **trust territories** under UN supervision in 1946.

**Trusteeship.** Britain and France were asked to administer British Cameroons and French Cameroun as **trust territories** and to prepare them for **self-government or independence**, with regular reports to the UN and visits by UN missions. This was different from the old mandate system because the UN had clearer goals of independence. The war had weakened Britain and France, and Africans who had fought for freedom abroad wanted freedom at home, so **nationalist movements** grew.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- The UN replaced the League of Nations; it did not continue it in the same form.
- Trusteeship did not mean immediate independence; it was a preparation period.
- Do not confuse the Second World War dates (1939–45) with those of the First World War (1914–18).

blocks.title: Example 1: causes
blocks.statement: Give two causes of the Second World War.
steps: Dictators such as Hitler pursued aggressive policies.
The League of Nations was too weak to stop them.
Economic depression and bitterness over Versailles also helped.
blocks.answer: Aggressive dictators and the weakness of the League (also the depression).

blocks.title: Example 2: effects on Cameroon
blocks.statement: Give two ways Cameroon contributed to the Allied war effort.
steps: It supplied men as soldiers and carriers.
It exported rubber, cocoa, timber and other products.
